He played college basketball for the [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State Beavers]]{{cite web|title=Ethan Thompson|url=http://www.osubeavers.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4159|website=OSUBeavers.com|access-date=October 31, 2023}} and represents the [[Puerto Rico men's national basketball team|Puerto Rican national team]]. ==High school career== Thompson played on Bishop Montgomery's varsity team for all 4 years during his high school career. As a senior at Bishop Montgomery he averaged 22.8 points, 7.7 rebounds, and 5.4 assists while also leading his team to the [[California Interscholastic Federation|CIF]] Open Division State Championship.{{cite web|title=2017 CIF State Boys Basketball Championships|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/tournament/oOM-kuG8EeaT-Oz0u-e-FA/oOM-k-G8EeaT-Oz0u-e-FA/basketball-winter-16-17/2017-cif-state-boys-basketball-championships--open-division-.htm|website=MaxPreps.com|access-date=September 20, 2024}} Bishop Montgomery beat [[Chino Hills High School|Chino Hills]], who were led by [[LaMelo Ball]] and his brother [[LiAngelo Ball|LiAngelo]], in the regional semi-finals, and beat [[Mater Dei High School (Santa Ana, California)|Mater Dei]] in the regional final before beating [[Woodcreek High School|Woodcreek]] to win the state title.{{cite news|first=Eric|last=Sondheimer|title=Open Division title belongs to the Bishop Montgomery Knights|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/highschool/varsity-times/la-sp-bishop-montgomery-woodcreek-20170325-story.html|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|date=March 25, 2017|access-date=September 17, 2017}} Thompson participated in the [[Ballislife All-American Game]] on May 6, 2017. He led the game in scoring with 32 points on 14-of-18 shooting.{{cite web|title=Ethan Thompson Scores A Game-High 32 Points In Ballislife All-American Game|url=https://www.buildingthedam.com/2017/5/6/15570774/ethan-thompson-scores-a-game-high-32-points-in-ballislife-all-american-game|website=BuildingTheDam.com|publisher=SB Nation|date=May 6, 2017|access-date=October 3, 2017}} ===Recruiting=== On November 9, 2016, Thompson signed his [[National Letter of Intent]] to play for [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State]], as he quoted, "I chose to attend OSU because I was impressed with the basketball facility, the coaching staff and the character of my future teammates. The opportunity to contribute as a freshman was appealing to me." {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2017}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Ethan Thompson | position = [[Shooting guard|SG]] | hometown = Los Angeles, CA | highschool = [[Bishop Montgomery High School|Bishop Montgomery]] (CA) | feet = 6 | inches = 5 | weight = 195 | 40 = | commitdate = September 19, 2016 | scout stars = 4 | rivals stars = 4 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 4 | espn grade = 88 }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = | year = 2017 | rivals ref title = Oregon State 2017 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2017 Oregon State Beavers Recruiting Class | 247 ref title = | rivals school = oregonstate | 247 school = | scout s = | espn schoolid = 204 | scout overall = 49 | rivals overall = 36 | 247 overall = 25 | espn overall = 41 | accessdate = September 17, 2017 | bball = yes }} ==College career== [[File:Ethan Thompson.jpg|thumb|upright|Thompson with [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State]] in 2020]] In his college debut against [[Southern Utah Thunderbirds men's basketball|Southern Utah]], Thompson scored 20 points, had 5 assists and grabbed 8 rebounds.{{cite web|title=Southern Utah vs. Oregon State – Game Summary – November 10, 2017 – ESPN|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game?gameId=400988191|website=ESPN.com|access-date=September 20, 2024}} On March 3, 2018, he scored a season-high 23 points in a 92–67 win over [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]].{{cite news|title=Ethan Thompson leads Oregon State to 25-point rout of Washington State|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/beavers/index.ssf/2018/03/ethan_thompson_leads_oregon_st.html|newspaper=The Oregonian|date=March 3, 2018|access-date=March 4, 2018}} After his sophomore season, Thompson declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]]. However, he withdrew from the draft on May 29, 2019, and returned to Oregon State for his junior season.{{cite news|title=OSU men's basketball: Ethan Thompson declares for NBA Draft|url=https://www.gazettetimes.com/sports/beavers-sports/basketball/osu-men-s-basketball-ethan-thompson-declares-for-nba-draft/article_329719ec-b7c4-578a-b3e8-23f3a1eb0a96.html|newspaper=[[Corvallis Gazette-Times]]|date=April 19, 2019|access-date=April 28, 2019}}{{cite web|title=Oregon State guard Ethan Thompson withdraws from NBA draft, returns to school for junior year — oregonlive.com|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/beavers/2019/05/oregon-state-guard-ethan-thompson-withdraws-from-nba-draft-returns-to-school-for-junior-year.html|website=OregonLive.com|date=May 30, 2019|access-date=September 20, 2024}} As a junior, Thompson started 31 games and finished second on the Beavers in scoring at 14.8 points a game, while leading the team in assists at 4.5 per game. Following the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]] but did not hire an agent.{{cite news|first=Nick|last=Daschel|title=Oregon State junior Ethan Thompson puts his name into the 2020 NBA Draft pool as an early entrant|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/beavers/2020/04/oregon-state-junior-ethan-thompson-puts-his-name-into-the-2020-nba-draft-pool-as-an-early-entrant.html|work=[[The Oregonian]]|date=April 27, 2020|access-date=May 1, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Windy City Bulls (2021–2023)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Thompson joined the [[Chicago Bulls]] for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|title=Bulls announce MGM Resorts NBA summer League 2021 roster|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-announce-mgm-resorts-nba-summer-league-2021-roster|website=NBA.com|date=August 4, 2021|access-date=August 4, 2021}} On September 8, 2021, he signed with the Bulls,{{cite web|title=Bulls sign free agents|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-free-agents|website=NBA.com|date=September 8, 2021|access-date=September 8, 2021}} but was waived on October 11.{{cite tweet|author=Chicago Bulls|title=Transactions: We have waived guard Ethan Thompson & center Daniel Oturu.|number=1447643169680728077|user=chicagobulls|date=October 11, 2021|access-date=October 11, 2021}} Thompson joined the [[Windy City Bulls]] as an affiliate player.{{cite web|first=Kyle|last=Brown|title=Windy City Bulls Announce Opening Night Roster|url=https://windycity.gleague.nba.com/news/windy-city-bulls-finalize-training-camp-roster-announce-basketball-operations-staff/|website=NBA.com|date=October 25, 2021|access-date=November 7, 2021}} ===Mexico City Capitanes (2023–2024)=== On October 30, 2023, Thompson signed with the [[Mexico City Capitanes]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite tweet|author=CAPITANES|title=Comunicado oficial: Capitanes presenta su roster para el Training Camp 23–24 #SomosCapitanes|number=1719057279763308852|user=CapitanesCDMX|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=October 31, 2023|language=Spanish}} ===Osos de Manatí (2024)=== On March 2, 2024, Thompson was selected first overall in the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|2024 BSN draft]] by the [[Osos de Manatí]].{{cite web|first=Carlos|last=González|title=Los Osos de Manatí fortalecen su plantilla con la selección de Ethan Thompson en el sorteo del BSN|url=https://www.elnuevodia.com/deportes/baloncesto/notas/los-osos-de-manati-fortalecen-su-plantilla-con-la-seleccion-de-ethan-thompson-en-el-sorteo-del-bsn/|website=ElNuevoDia.com|date=March 2, 2024|access-date=March 19, 2024|language=Spanish}} ===Osceola Magic (2024–2025)=== On September 20, 2024, Thompson signed with the [[Orlando Magic]],{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Sign Free Agents Mac McClung, Javonte Smart and Ethan Thompson|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-sign-free-agents-mac-mcclung-javonte-smart-ethan-thompson-20240919|website=NBA.com|date=September 20, 2024|access-date=September 20, 2024}} but was waived on October 19.{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Convert Contract of Mac McClung to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-convert-contract-of-mac-mcclung-to-two-way-contract-20241019|website=NBA.com|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 21, 2024}} Eight days later, he joined the [[Osceola Magic]].{{cite web|title=Osceola Magic Announce Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/osceola-magic-announce-training-camp-roster/n-6160339|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 27, 2024|access-date=October 27, 2024}} On February 7, 2025, Thompson signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Orlando Magic where he split time with the NBA club and its G-League affiliate.{{Cite web|title=Orlando Magic Sign Ethan Thompson to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-sign-ethan-thompson-to-two-way-contract-20250207|access-date=November 13, 2025|website=nba.com|language=en}} However, he did not appear for Orlando during his time with the team. On July 23, Thompson was waived by the Magic.{{Cite web|title=Orlando Magic Waive Ethan Thompson From Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.si.com/nba/magic/onsi/orlando-magic-waive-ethan-thompson-from-two-way-contract-01k0wkq9xx17|access-date=November 13, 2025|website=si.com|date=July 23, 2025 |language=en}} ===Sioux Falls Skyforce (2025)=== On August 14, 2025, Thompson signed an [[Exhibit 10]] contract with the [[Miami Heat]].{{Cite web|title=Heat Sign Ethan Thompson|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-ethan-thompson|access-date=November 13, 2025|website=nba.com|language=en}} He was waived by the Heat prior to the start of the regular season on October 17. He would sign with the Heat’s [[NBA G League|G-League]] affiliate, the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]]. {{Cite web|title=Ethan Thompson: Waived Friday|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/ethan-thompson-waived-friday/|access-date=November 13, 2025|website=cbssports.com|date=October 18, 2025 |language=en}} In his eight games with the Skyforce he averaged 26.9 points, 5.8 rebounds and 6.5 assists per game. {{Cite web |last=Dopirak |first=Dustin |title=Pacers give Ethan Thompson NBA debut opportunity: 'Heart was racing' |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2025/12/05/pacers-ethan-thompson-nba-debut-rookie/87603604007/ |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=The Indianapolis Star |language=en-US}} ===Indiana Pacers / Noblesville Boom (2025–2026)=== On December 1, 2025, Thompson signed a two-way contract with the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{Cite web |title=The Indiana Pacers Sign Ethan Thompson to a Two-Way Contract |url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/the-indiana-pacers-sign-ethan-thompson-to-a-two-way-contract |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=The NBA G League |language=en}} Thompson made his NBA debut against the [[2025–26 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cleveland Cavaliers]] that day, scoring his first career points on a jump shot in the 4th quarter.{{Cite web |title=Cavaliers vs Pacers, December 1, 2025 |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/pbp/202512010IND.html |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} On December 5, Thompson would score a career-high 11 points, while also registering two rebounds, three assists, one steal, and two blocks. On December 8, Thompson would make his first career start against the [[2025–26 Sacramento Kings season|Sacramento Kings]]; he finished the game with six points and five rebounds.{{Cite web |title=Ethan Thompson 2025-26 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/t/thompet01/gamelog/2026/ |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} On April 1, 2026, Thompson scored a career high 24 points on 8-of-15 shooting from the field, and added 5 assists in an 145–126 victory against the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{Cite Web |title=Ethan Thompson Scores 24 |url=https://8points9seconds.com/ethan-thompson-just-sent-pacers-important-reminder |access-date=2026-04-01 |website=8points9seconds.com |language=en}} ===Partizan (2026–present)=== On August 16, 2026, Thompson signed a two-year deal with [[KK Partizan|Partizan]] of the [[Basketball League of Serbia|Serbian SuperLeague]], the [[ABA League]], and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite news|title=Itan Tompson je osmo pojačanje Partizana Mozzart Bet ovog leta|url=https://partizan.basketball/vesti/aktuelno/4232|date=August 16, 2026|website=partizan.basketball|access-date=August 16, 2026|language=sr}} ==National team career== Thompson played for [[Puerto Rico national basketball team|Puerto Rico]] at the [[2016 FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]]. Thompson averaged 11.8 points, 6.2 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game in the tournament.[https://web.archive.org/web/20180131081111/http://www.archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/130783/pid2/106956/sid/8094/tid/349/tid2/261/_/2016_FIBA_Americas_U18_Championship_for_Men/index.html
